claims.canonical_statement: The accepted scientific name is Monstera deliciosa Liebm.
claims.confidence_rationale: POWO directly records the species as accepted; IPNI independently confirms the nomenclatural name, authorship and original publication.
claims.publication_rationale: Taxonomy Review exists but awaits a human reviewer.
claims.publishable_wording: Nom accepté : Monstera deliciosa Liebm.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT: current Jungle value is correct but was not Evidence-linked.

claims.canonical_statement: Monstera deliciosa belongs to genus Monstera, family Araceae, order Alismatales.
claims.confidence_rationale: Direct POWO classification; IPNI confirms family as entered.
claims.publication_rationale: Pending human taxonomy review.
claims.publishable_wording: Araceae · Monstera · Alismatales.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT: matches current Jungle.

claims.canonical_statement: Monstera borsigiana K.Koch is treated by POWO as a synonym of Monstera deliciosa, not as a separate accepted species.
claims.confidence_rationale: Direct synonymy entry in the authoritative taxonomic backbone.
claims.publication_rationale: Human taxonomy review required before changing comparison copy.
claims.publishable_wording: « Monstera borsigiana » est aujourd'hui traité par POWO comme un synonyme de Monstera deliciosa, et non comme une espèce distincte.
claims.legacy_comparison: SUPERSEDES current Jungle comparison that presents borsigiana as a separate look-alike.

claims.canonical_statement: Philodendron pertusum is listed by POWO among the synonyms of Monstera deliciosa.
claims.confidence_rationale: Direct POWO synonymy record.
claims.publication_rationale: Pending taxonomy review.
claims.publishable_wording: Philodendron pertusum est un nom historique placé en synonymie, pas le nom accepté actuel.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT: current Jungle lists it without evidentiary context.

claims.canonical_statement: POWO records the native range as southern Mexico (Veracruz, Oaxaca and Chiapas) to Guatemala.
claims.confidence_rationale: Direct native-range record from POWO.
claims.publication_rationale: Other horticultural sources broaden the range to Costa Rica/Panama; POWO is authoritative for native range and the editorial wording should avoid blending native and introduced/cultivated ranges.
claims.publishable_wording: Aire native documentée par POWO : sud du Mexique — notamment Veracruz, Oaxaca et Chiapas — jusqu'au Guatemala.
claims.legacy_comparison: QUALIFIES current 'Mexique à Amérique centrale', which is too broad.

claims.canonical_statement: Monstera deliciosa primarily grows in the wet tropical biome.
claims.confidence_rationale: Direct POWO biome field.
claims.publication_rationale: Stable botanical fact; editorial review still pending.
claims.publishable_wording: Biome principal : tropical humide.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT and more precise than current generic habitat copy.

claims.canonical_statement: Monstera deliciosa is a climbing liana that uses supports in forest habitats.
claims.confidence_rationale: POWO identifies a liana; RHS, NC State and UF/IFAS independently describe climbing habit/support use.
claims.publication_rationale: Can be considered after editorial review.
claims.publishable_wording: C'est une liane grimpante : dans son milieu, elle progresse en s'appuyant sur des supports végétaux.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT: supports current climbing description.

claims.canonical_statement: Monstera is described in botanical literature as a secondary hemiepiphytic climbing lineage; applying that label to M. deliciosa is supported but should retain context.
claims.confidence_rationale: Muir and Croat support the life form mainly at genus level; NC State describes the species starting terrestrially then becoming epiphytic upon reaching a support.
claims.publication_rationale: The terminology is technical and part of the evidence is genus-level.
claims.publishable_wording: Son développement est souvent décrit comme secondairement hémiépiphyte : elle débute au sol puis grimpe sur un support, tout en conservant une relation avec le sol selon son stade et son milieu.
claims.legacy_comparison: QUALIFIES current unqualified 'hémiepiphyte secondaire'.

claims.canonical_statement: Monstera exhibits marked ontogenetic changes in leaf form (heteroblasty), with juvenile and mature leaves differing substantially.
claims.confidence_rationale: Croat and Muir explicitly discuss heteroblasty in Monstera; NC State independently distinguishes mature perforated leaves.
claims.publication_rationale: Suitable after editorial review with stage qualifiers.
claims.publishable_wording: La forme des feuilles change avec le développement : les feuilles juvéniles et adultes ne présentent pas la même découpe.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT: supports the current juvenile-to-adult narrative.

claims.canonical_statement: Mature Monstera deliciosa leaves can develop both margin-reaching divisions and internal perforations.
claims.confidence_rationale: Specific descriptions from NC State and UF/IFAS converge; Muir treats adult fenestration as the defining trait under study.
claims.publication_rationale: Ready for editorial review.
claims.publishable_wording: À maturité, les feuilles peuvent présenter à la fois des découpes atteignant le bord et des perforations internes.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT and more precise than 'trous'.

claims.canonical_statement: The adaptive function of Monstera leaf fenestration is not established as a single proven fact; Muir proposes a model-based growth-variance hypothesis for patchy understory light.
claims.confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed modeling paper explicitly frames the result as a testable hypothesis and reviews competing conjectures.
claims.publication_rationale: Must not be simplified into a certain evolutionary function.
claims.publishable_wording: La fonction évolutive des fenestrations n'est pas démontrée par une explication unique. Une hypothèse scientifique propose qu'elles répartissent mieux la lumière intermittente du sous-bois, mais elle reste à tester.
claims.legacy_comparison: REJECTS any categorical explanation such as 'holes let light reach lower leaves' as established fact.

claims.canonical_statement: Maturity is clearly associated with fenestration; brighter filtered light and climbing support are horticulturally associated with more mature leaf form, but neither should be presented as a guaranteed single trigger.
claims.confidence_rationale: Maturity is corroborated by morphology sources; RHS and UConn give horticultural associations for light/support without controlled causal proof.
claims.publication_rationale: Causal wording must remain guarded.
claims.publishable_wording: L'absence de fenestrations est d'abord compatible avec un stade juvénile. Une lumière filtrée suffisante et un support adapté favorisent une croissance plus mature, sans garantir à eux seuls l'apparition de découpes.
claims.legacy_comparison: QUALIFIES current 'maturité, lumière et support' causal shorthand.

claims.canonical_statement: For indoor cultivation, bright or moderate indirect/filtered light is consistently recommended; strong direct sun can scorch leaves.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS profile/guide and NC State independently converge; UConn's regional partial-sun guidance reinforces the need for acclimation/context rather than a universal direct-sun prohibition.
claims.publication_rationale: Publishable after editorial review without lux/hour precision.
claims.publishable_wording: Placez-la dans une lumière lumineuse à modérée, filtrée ou indirecte. Un soleil direct intense peut brûler le feuillage ; toute exposition plus forte demande une acclimatation progressive.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT; legacy score 4/5 remains an editorial score, not evidence.

claims.canonical_statement: Water thoroughly after the upper portion of the potting medium has dried appreciably; do not use a fixed calendar interval.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS says allow compost to become almost dry; NC State specifies the upper quarter to third; UConn gives 2–3 inches. They converge on substrate state but differ in operational threshold.
claims.publication_rationale: Use qualitative wording and retain context.
claims.publishable_wording: Contrôlez le substrat plutôt que le calendrier : laissez sa partie supérieure sécher nettement, puis arrosez à fond et laissez l'excédent s'écouler.
claims.legacy_comparison: REPLACES generic 'arroser tous les 10–15 jours'; legacy 2/5 is editorial only.

claims.canonical_statement: Prolonged saturation or standing water increases the risk of root and stem rot.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS and UConn independently connect persistent wetness/standing water with rot risk.
claims.publication_rationale: Low-risk guidance after editorial review.
claims.publishable_wording: Ne laissez pas le pot baigner durablement dans l'eau : un milieu constamment saturé augmente le risque de pourriture racinaire.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT.

claims.canonical_statement: Monstera deliciosa prefers moderate-to-high or humid air, but the evidence reviewed does not establish a universal required relative-humidity range.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS and NC State independently state a qualitative preference; no opened authoritative source validates the historical 50–75% band as a species requirement.
claims.publication_rationale: Qualitative wording only.
claims.publishable_wording: Elle apprécie un air modérément à assez humide, mais ce n'est pas une raison pour présenter une plage universelle obligatoire.
claims.legacy_comparison: REJECTS exact 50–75% range as insufficiently evidenced.

claims.canonical_statement: The historical Jungle range 50–75% RH is not sufficiently supported as a universal Monstera deliciosa requirement.
claims.confidence_rationale: Opened institutional sources use qualitative terms; none supports both bounds in the same context.
claims.publication_rationale: Numeric precision is unsupported.
claims.legacy_comparison: LEGACY value should be deprecated, not silently retained.

claims.canonical_statement: Institutional indoor guidance consistently favors warm conditions, but exact bands vary: RHS gives 18–25°C while NC State gives 60–85°F (about 15.6–29.4°C).
claims.confidence_rationale: Reliable sources converge qualitatively but not on identical numeric bounds.
claims.publication_rationale: Owner/editorial decision required before publishing any exact range.
claims.publishable_wording: Conservez-la au chaud et à l'écart des courants d'air froids. Les guides institutionnels consultés donnent des plages différentes selon leur contexte ; évitez d'en faire une limite universelle.
claims.legacy_comparison: QUALIFIES 18–28°C; exact legacy range is not directly corroborated.

claims.canonical_statement: A universal minimum of 15°C is not established by the reviewed evidence; sources distinguish preferred indoor warmth, outdoor handling and cold-damage thresholds.
claims.confidence_rationale: NC State's lower preferred bound approximates 15.6°C, RHS gives 18°C or 18–25°C, UConn uses 45°F/7.2°C for summer outdoor handling, and UF/IFAS gives freeze-damage thresholds; these are not equivalent endpoints.
claims.publication_rationale: Would conflate optimum, handling minimum and damage threshold.
claims.legacy_comparison: LEGACY numeric minimum should be replaced by contextual warm/cold guidance.

claims.canonical_statement: Container media should be open/aerated, well drained and retain some organic matter/moisture without remaining saturated.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS and UConn converge on open/well-drained and organic-rich media; rot guidance supports avoiding persistent saturation.
claims.publication_rationale: Publish properties, not an invented percentage recipe.
claims.publishable_wording: Visez un substrat ouvert, aéré et drainant, contenant de la matière organique mais ne restant pas saturé.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT; legacy ingredient list remains a Tibaldo recipe unless separately documented.

claims.canonical_statement: Use a container that permits drainage and increase size incrementally rather than overpotting.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS and UConn independently warn against disproportionate container size and persistent wetness.
claims.publication_rationale: Low-risk guidance after editorial review.
claims.publishable_wording: Choisissez un contenant drainant, seulement un peu plus grand que la motte ; un pot surdimensionné reste humide plus longtemps.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT.

claims.canonical_statement: Repotting is justified by rootball/container fit and stability, not a rigid annual schedule; roots reaching the pot's bottom and sides are a direct check.
claims.confidence_rationale: UConn gives a direct root inspection criterion; RHS discusses rootball fit and top-heaviness while providing only a broad timing tendency.
claims.publication_rationale: Prefer observed signs over frequency.
claims.publishable_wording: Rempotez lorsque les racines occupent réellement le contenant — notamment lorsqu'elles atteignent le fond et les côtés — ou lorsque la stabilité devient insuffisante, plutôt que selon un calendrier rigide.
claims.legacy_comparison: QUALIFIES generic 'every 2–3 years'.

claims.canonical_statement: Balanced fertiliser is recommended during active growth; exact frequency differs among institutional sources.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS guide/profile converge on balanced feed in growth, with one specifying monthly; UConn cautions about salts and gives regional active-growth months.
claims.publication_rationale: A universal frequency/dilution is not established.
claims.publishable_wording: Fertilisez modérément pendant la croissance active avec un engrais équilibré, en suivant le dosage du produit et en évitant l'accumulation de sels. La fréquence dépend du produit et des conditions réelles.
claims.legacy_comparison: QUALIFIES generic 'monthly half-strength'.

claims.canonical_statement: Vegetative propagation by stem cutting requires stem tissue containing at least one node; a detached leaf without a node is not supported as a method for producing a complete new plant.
claims.confidence_rationale: UConn's species-specific cutting instruction locates the cut below a node; Iowa State's protocol requires nodes and explicitly lists M. deliciosa as suitable for stem cuttings.
claims.publication_rationale: The 'leaf alone' conclusion is limited to the absence of supported complete-plant propagation, not a claim that a leaf can never form adventitious roots.
claims.publishable_wording: Pour obtenir une nouvelle plante par bouture de tige, conservez au moins un nœud. Une feuille isolée sans nœud ne constitue pas une bouture de tige viable pour reformer une plante complète.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT and clarifies generic propagation copy.

claims.canonical_statement: A support helps manage the natural climbing habit and physical stability; associations with larger, more mature leaves are documented horticulturally but are not a guaranteed fenestration switch.
claims.confidence_rationale: NC State directly supports physical stability; RHS and UConn associate climbing with mature/larger leaves; controlled causality is not established.
claims.publication_rationale: Publish only with non-guarantee qualifier.
claims.publishable_wording: Un support accompagne son port grimpant et stabilise les tiges. Il peut favoriser l'expression d'une croissance plus mature, sans garantir à lui seul de grandes feuilles ou des fenestrations.
claims.legacy_comparison: QUALIFIES support=few holes causal implication.

claims.canonical_statement: Aerial roots arise from vine nodes and contribute to anchorage/climbing; they may continue growing and can root on contacting suitable ground or substrate.
claims.confidence_rationale: UF/IFAS specifically describes emergence and rooting on ground contact; RHS describes rooting into a moist support; peer-reviewed work confirms distinct aerial-root growth/anatomy.
claims.publication_rationale: Botanical role is supportable after editorial review.
claims.publishable_wording: Les racines aériennes participent à l'ancrage et à la progression de la liane ; au contact d'un milieu favorable, certaines peuvent s'y enraciner.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT.

claims.canonical_statement: The reviewed direct evidence is insufficient to issue a universal rule that aerial roots should always be cut, never cut, or always guided into the pot.
claims.confidence_rationale: Opened sources document role/anatomy but not a controlled universal home-practice rule.
claims.publication_rationale: Needs a directly relevant horticultural source or owner-labelled practice.
claims.legacy_comparison: Legacy 'guide them, shorten only if necessary' remains unverified guidance.

claims.canonical_statement: Reported dimensions depend strongly on context: outdoor/wild-like vines may exceed 21 m in length, RHS gives 4–8 m under its horticultural profile, and NC State gives about 1.8–2.4 m in most home environments.
claims.confidence_rationale: Institutional sources directly give values but for non-equivalent settings.
claims.publication_rationale: Must separate potential vine length from typical indoor height.
claims.publishable_wording: La liane peut dépasser 20 m dans des conditions extérieures favorables ; en intérieur, elle reste généralement bien plus contenue, souvent autour de quelques mètres selon l'espace, le support et la taille.
claims.legacy_comparison: REPLACES vague 'several meters' with contextual categories.

claims.canonical_statement: Monstera deliciosa is described as vigorous or fast growing in favorable horticultural/outdoor contexts, but no universal indoor growth rate is established.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS describes vigorous plants and UF/IFAS fast outdoor vine growth; neither defines a transferable indoor rate.
claims.publication_rationale: Growth speed depends on light, temperature, root zone, stage and support.
claims.publishable_wording: Sa croissance peut être vigoureuse lorsque les conditions sont favorables, mais sa vitesse réelle en intérieur varie fortement avec la lumière, la chaleur, l'espace racinaire et le support.
claims.legacy_comparison: QUALIFIES legacy 'rapide'.

claims.canonical_statement: Monstera deliciosa contains insoluble needle-like calcium oxalate crystals associated with oral and contact irritation.
claims.confidence_rationale: ASPCA directly identifies insoluble calcium oxalates in the species; NC State independently identifies needle-like calcium oxalate crystals and contact dermatitis.
claims.publication_rationale: All Safety claims require human Safety Review.
claims.publishable_wording: La plante contient des cristaux insolubles d'oxalate de calcium pouvant irriter la bouche, les muqueuses et, chez certaines personnes, la peau.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT and more precise than generic 'irritating sap'.

claims.canonical_statement: Chewing oxalate-containing plant tissue can cause acute oral pain, irritation, swelling and difficulty swallowing; keep Monstera deliciosa out of children's reach and seek professional poison-control/medical advice for concerning exposure.
claims.confidence_rationale: NC State is species-specific; CHOP provides direct institutional mechanism and symptom guidance for oxalate plants generally; RHS advises keeping the species away from children.
claims.publication_rationale: Safety Review pending; public wording must avoid diagnosis or treatment protocol.
claims.publishable_wording: Gardez la plante hors de portée des enfants. En cas de mastication ou d'irritation importante — notamment gonflement ou difficulté à avaler — contactez un centre antipoison ou un professionnel de santé.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT with professional-referral guardrail.

claims.canonical_statement: ASPCA classifies Monstera deliciosa as toxic to dogs and cats; chewing can cause oral irritation, drooling, vomiting and difficulty swallowing.
claims.confidence_rationale: Direct species-specific ASPCA Animal Poison Control profile.
claims.publication_rationale: Safety Review remains mandatory despite strong evidence.
claims.publishable_wording: Toxique pour les chiens et les chats en cas de mastication. Une irritation buccale, une salivation excessive, des vomissements ou une difficulté à avaler peuvent survenir ; contactez un vétérinaire ou un centre antipoison vétérinaire si une exposition est suspectée.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT.

claims.canonical_statement: Scale insects and spider mites are directly documented for Monstera deliciosa; UConn additionally documents mealybugs and aphids. Thrips are plausible houseplant pests but were not directly documented for this species in the opened species-specific sources.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS/UConn provide species-specific pest records; the opened thrips source is general-domain only.
claims.publication_rationale: Thrips must remain qualified until a direct source is opened.
claims.publishable_wording: Surveillez surtout les cochenilles et les acariens, directement documentés sur cette espèce. Les cochenilles farineuses sont également signalées. Les thrips restent une hypothèse à confirmer par inspection, pas un diagnostic automatique.
claims.legacy_comparison: QUALIFIES current direct listing of thrips as species-established.

claims.canonical_statement: Fine stippling, bronzing/bleaching and webbing are compatible with spider mites; inspect leaf undersides with magnification or tap over white paper.
claims.confidence_rationale: UConn gives species-specific signs; UMN provides independent diagnostic procedure for twospotted mites.
claims.publication_rationale: Diagnostic language remains probabilistic.
claims.publishable_wording: De fines ponctuations claires et des toiles peuvent évoquer des acariens. Vérifiez le revers des feuilles à la loupe ou secouez une feuille au-dessus d'un papier blanc avant d'agir.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT with verification step.

claims.canonical_statement: Yellow leaves are non-specific. Possible causes include root-zone saturation/rot, pest feeding, disease, cold or natural leaf senescence; diagnosis requires checking substrate, roots, temperature history and pests.
claims.confidence_rationale: UConn directly documents yellowing from scale/mealybugs and root/stem rot signs; RHS supports wet-root risk. Natural senescence is general plant biology but was not found in a species-specific source during this pilot.
claims.publication_rationale: Some possible causes remain general-domain; no single-cause diagnosis is supportable.
claims.publishable_wording: Une feuille jaune ne suffit pas à conclure. Contrôlez d'abord l'humidité du substrat, l'état des racines, les températures récentes et la présence de ravageurs ; une vieille feuille isolée peut aussi simplement terminer son cycle.
claims.legacy_comparison: REPLACES categorical legacy cause list with a verification pathway.

claims.canonical_statement: Brown edges or patches are non-specific; dry air or direct-sun scorch are supported possibilities, while patterned lesions, yellow margins or ooze require disease assessment.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS links dry air and direct sun to browning/scorch; UConn describes bacterial/anthracnose lesion patterns.
claims.publication_rationale: Requires observable pattern qualifiers; salts and irregular watering remain insufficiently evidenced in opened species-specific sources.
claims.publishable_wording: Des bords bruns peuvent être compatibles avec un air très sec ou une brûlure lumineuse. Si les taches s'étendent, présentent un halo jaune ou un suintement, isolez la plante et faites préciser le diagnostic.
claims.legacy_comparison: QUALIFIES legacy list; WITHHOLDS salts/irregular watering as species-specific facts.

claims.canonical_statement: Slow growth or smaller leaves may reflect low light, seasonal/temperature context, root-zone constraint or a return to less mature growth after pruning; support is an association, not a guaranteed cure.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS links low light and post-pruning growth to less mature leaves; UConn links support attachment with leaf-size increase; root constraints and temperature need contextual inspection.
claims.publication_rationale: No single diagnosis; some factors are associations.
claims.publishable_wording: Une croissance ralentie ou de petites feuilles demandent de vérifier ensemble la lumière, la saison, la température, l'espace racinaire et le port de la plante. Un support peut accompagner la maturité, mais ne constitue pas une correction garantie.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT and de-categorised.

claims.canonical_statement: Lack of fenestrations is compatible with juvenile stage and can also be associated with insufficient light or non-climbing growth; it is not evidence of a single fault.
claims.confidence_rationale: Stage is corroborated; light/support associations come from institutional horticultural guidance.
claims.publication_rationale: Avoid support/light guarantees.
claims.publishable_wording: Des feuilles sans fenestrations peuvent être normales sur une plante jeune. Vérifiez aussi si la lumière est suffisante et si la liane peut grimper, sans promettre qu'un tuteur fera apparaître les découpes.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT with explicit non-guarantee.

claims.canonical_statement: Stems can be pruned to control size; pruning may be followed by smaller, less mature leaves during regrowth.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS and UF/IFAS independently support stem pruning for size; RHS supplies the regrowth qualifier.
claims.publication_rationale: Cleaning tool hygiene remains a general-domain practice requiring separate evidence if stated.
claims.publishable_wording: Vous pouvez raccourcir les tiges pour contenir la plante. La repousse peut d'abord produire des feuilles plus petites et moins matures.
claims.legacy_comparison: REBUILT.

claims.canonical_statement: Wiping accumulated dust from leaves is recommended as routine care and also provides an opportunity to inspect for pests.
claims.confidence_rationale: RHS recommends regular wiping for dust/insect inspection; NC State independently recommends wiping dust from leaves.
claims.publication_rationale: Low-risk routine care after editorial review; no leaf-shine product is implied.
claims.publishable_wording: Essuyez doucement la poussière avec un support propre et profitez-en pour examiner le revers des feuilles. Aucun produit lustrant n'est nécessaire.
claims.legacy_comparison: NEW_EVIDENCE_CLAIM; no dedicated current Jungle claim located.

claims.canonical_statement: The Jungle light score 4/5 is an editorial construct, not a botanical measurement.
claims.confidence_rationale: No scoring rubric is present in Evidence V1.
claims.publication_rationale: Requires a future Owner-approved editorial rubric.
claims.legacy_comparison: LEGACY_UNVERIFIED editorial score.

claims.canonical_statement: The Jungle watering score 2/5 is an editorial construct, not a botanical measurement.
claims.confidence_rationale: No scoring rubric is present in Evidence V1.
claims.publication_rationale: Requires a future Owner-approved editorial rubric.
claims.legacy_comparison: LEGACY_UNVERIFIED editorial score.

claims.canonical_statement: The Jungle humidity score 3/5 is an editorial construct, not a botanical measurement.
claims.confidence_rationale: No scoring rubric is present in Evidence V1.
claims.publication_rationale: Requires a future Owner-approved editorial rubric.
claims.legacy_comparison: LEGACY_UNVERIFIED editorial score.

claims.canonical_statement: The Jungle difficulty score 2/5 is an editorial construct, not a botanical fact.
claims.confidence_rationale: No explicit documented scoring criteria have been applied.
claims.publication_rationale: Future Content Master/Owner review may derive a score from objective claims.
claims.legacy_comparison: LEGACY_UNVERIFIED editorial score.

claims.canonical_statement: Evidence exists to answer placement, watering trigger, lack of fenestrations, repotting trigger, drained-container and toxicity questions cautiously; universal aerial-root cutting guidance remains unsupported.
claims.confidence_rationale: This is a coverage assessment derived from the atomic claims, not a final FAQ.
claims.publication_rationale: The mission explicitly forbids producing the final FAQ.
claims.legacy_comparison: Current FAQ can be rebuilt later from approved claims; it is not approved here.
